title: Tata Capital Ltd - 544574 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Tata Capital Q2 FY27 consolidated AUM rose 26% YoY to INR3,08,030 crore and PAT grew 51% YoY to INR1,660 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated AUM crossed INR3 lakh crore, growing 26% YoY and 6% QoQ, with 32% YoY growth excluding Motor Finance. PAT rose 51% YoY to INR1,660 crore, ROA was 2.3% (2.5% ex-Motor Finance) and ROE exceeded 14%. Credit cost eased to 0.9% from 1.0% in Q1 and Stage 3 was stable at 1.9%, while NIM plus fee fell about 10 bps QoQ. Management guided to a 25 bps repo hike in October and a 20-25 bps PLR increase effective 1 November, and said it expects no further NIM plus fee drag in Q3 and a distinct improvement in Q4. Revolving credit and insurance commission regulations remain open risks, with no quantification given.

segments.name: Tata Capital Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR95,098 crore (+26% YoY, +6% QoQ), PAT INR552 crore, ROA 2.5%, ROE 18%. Affordable and micro housing AUM grew 22% YoY and 5% QoQ; 23 new locations added in the quarter.

segments.name: Retail and SME
segments.commentary: Retail and SME make up 85.4% of consolidated AUM. Supply chain has diversified, with auto now about 35% of supply chain versus about two-thirds four years ago.

segments.name: High-margin businesses
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 40% YoY while AUM growth rose to 14% from 10% in Q1; management expects AUM growth to reach overall portfolio levels by Q4.

segments.name: Motor Finance (TMFL)
segments.commentary: Portfolio is still running down, with the Q2 rundown below Q1 and Q1 below Q4 FY26. Management expects stabilisation in Q3 and growth from Q4. Share of the book fell from 14.5% in March 2025 to about 7.7%. Gross NPA rise is attributed to seasonality and a shrinking denominator; absolute Q2 slippages were lower YoY. A macro provision of about INR30 crore was created in CV.

segments.name: Microfinance and flexi loans
segments.commentary: Microfinance is under 1% of the book, with improving asset quality and growth. Retail flexi loans are about 2-2.5% of the book. Management estimates the revolving credit impact at 3-4% of AUM if products cannot be converted.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 23-25% for FY27 and over FY25-FY28; management says it will land within this range and is not looking to revise guidance down.
Management is not revising FY28 ROA and ROE guidance and says it may revise upward at year-end; it is confident of meeting cost-to-income, credit cost and PAT growth guidance.
PLR increase of 25 bps (standalone ALCO) and 20 bps (Housing Finance) effective 1 November 2026, to protect NIM plus fee.
NIM plus fee expected stable in Q3 FY27 and improving distinctly in Q4 FY27.
Management expects about 2 further repo hikes in FY27 (market talk of around 50 bps more).
Income growth expected around 25% and cost growth around 15% for the year.
Capital raise expected in H2 FY28, more towards Q3-Q4, based on the current growth plan.
capex_capacity: Branch network at about 1,515 branches across 1,094 locations in 26 states and UTs; net addition of 24 branches in Q2.
Q3 and Q4 location expansion in affordable and micro housing planned to be stronger than Q2.
Gold loan business is not yet live; launch expected in the coming month.
On-roll employee strength 31,655, with over 80% in frontline sales and collections; headcount up 6% against AUM up 26%.
Over 180 digital partnerships; 9.2 million customers served.
demand_pricing: Management described festive demand as strong across two-wheeler, passenger vehicle and commercial vehicle segments, with dealer supply-chain demand also rising.
Rural growth is slower than urban, but Tata Capital's rural exposure is limited to microfinance; it has no tractor or agri farm loans and hardly any microfinance in Maharashtra.
Housing NIM fell about 5 bps QoQ from competitive pressure in prime home loans; the other 5 bps came from higher cost of funds.
Fee income rose 30% YoY, driven by assignment income (DA income up 58% YoY); non-assignment fee income held at Q1 level as a percentage of AUM.
Management is declining some deals that do not meet margin requirements, prioritising margins over growth.
Floating-rate liabilities are 48% of total liabilities and floating-rate assets 66% of assets.

qa_highlights.question: Path if revolving credit draft norms are adopted, and whether exposure is being cut before final norms.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not cut exposure and is piloting alternate products, with more to start in November; it estimates the impact at 3-4% of AUM and believes more than half of flexi can be converted to modified products at similar pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Insurance distribution norms impact and alternative fee sources.
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not quantified the impact, which depends on final regulations. Options include selling retail insurance, growing NIM plus fee, and reducing costs if insurance is not sold.

qa_highlights.question: Motor Finance NPA rise and the timing of book growth.
qa_highlights.answer: The rise reflects seasonality (Q2 typically has the highest NPA growth) and a shrinking denominator; absolute slippages were lower YoY. Portfolio growth is expected to stabilise in Q3 and resume in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: NIM trajectory for H2 FY27 and FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: NIM fell about 10 bps QoQ in Q2 (about 5 bps from cost of funds and 5 bps from prime home loan competition). Management expects stability in Q3 and a distinct improvement in Q4, and says a rate increase should be neutral to accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the SME growth is channel finance and whether supply-chain growth will shift to retail.
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from both term loans and supply chain, with supply chain having a particularly strong quarter. Auto is about 35% of supply chain, down from about two-thirds four years ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capital raise timing.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to need capital in H2 FY28, more towards Q3-Q4, and will also consider sub-debt; it did not give a precise size.

qa_highlights.question: Why yields are not rising despite high-margin growth.
qa_highlights.answer: Balance transfer pressure eases in a rising-rate environment, and high-margin AUM growth (14%) is expected to reach overall portfolio growth by Q4. Business-level yield plans are expected to show output from end-Q3 or Q4.

risks_watch: Revolving credit (flexi) and insurance commission regulations could hit fee income and product economics; no quantification given yet.
Repo hikes and tighter liquidity (surplus down below INR1 lakh crore) could push cost of funds higher than the 20-25 bps PLR pass-through.
Motor Finance: Q3 stabilisation and Q4 growth are not yet demonstrated; NPA trend is seasonal.
Drought, fuel prices and CV utilisation could affect the CV book and the rural and microfinance exposure.
Capital: CRAR has fallen about 100 bps per quarter since IPO, with a capital raise expected in H2 FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics and guidance, with explicit reassurance that FY28 targets are unchanged. Noticeably cautious and non-committal on revolving credit and insurance regulation, saying the impact cannot be quantified. Defensive on the Motor Finance growth lag and the Q2 NIM dip.
key_quotes: We do not want growth at the expense of margins.
We expect the portfolio to stabilize in Q3 and start growing from Q4.
We remain on track to deliver our medium-term guidance with operating leverage expected to be an important lever of further improvement in ROA.
Insurance remains an important risk cover for our customers and an integral part of our underwriting framework.

growth.why: AUM growth guidance of 23-25% for FY27 held, with income growth guided around 25% and cost growth around 15%; backing is partial (branch and location expansion, gold loan launch, strong festive demand, and a PLR hike to protect NIM), with no quantified order or capacity book behind the guidance.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM plus fee fell about 10 bps QoQ in Q2 (5 bps cost of funds, 5 bps prime home loan competition); management guides stable in Q3 and a distinct improvement in Q4, with the 25 bps PLR hike to protect NIM.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network at about 1,515 branches after 24 net adds in Q2, with Q3 and Q4 affordable/micro housing location expansion guided stronger than Q2 and a gold loan launch expected within a month.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM growth guided at 23-25% for FY27 and management says it will land within that range; AUM is up 26% YoY and disbursements up 29% YoY, with 32% growth ex-Motor Finance.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says FY28 ROA and ROE may be revised upward at year-end; ROE is above 14% and ROA is 2.3% (2.5% ex-Motor Finance), but no near-term raise is guided.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revolving credit (flexi, 2-2.5% of book, 3-4% of AUM impact if not converted) and insurance commission rules are unquantified, and Motor Finance growth resumes only from Q4 with Q3 stabilisation not yet shown.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gold loan business is approved but not yet live, with launch expected in the coming month; alternate flexi products start in November as a pilot.

rows.label: PLR hike of 25 bps (standalone) and 20 bps (Housing) from 1 Nov 2026
rows.why: Effective 1 November 2026 to protect NIM plus fee against about 25 bps of repo hikes, with management saying a rate rise should be neutral to accretive.

rows.label: Capital raise in H2 FY28
rows.why: CRAR has fallen about 100 bps per quarter since IPO (standalone 17.3%, CET1 14.7%), and management expects to raise capital more towards Q3-Q4 FY28, possibly alongside sub-debt.

rows.label: Revolving credit and insurance commission norms
rows.why: Flexi loans are 2-2.5% of book with a 3-4% of AUM impact if not converted; management believes over half can be converted at similar pricing, and insurance impact is not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on AUM guidance (23-25%), FY28 targets and the PLR pass-through, but cautious and non-committal on revolving credit and insurance rules and defensive on Motor Finance's growth lag and the Q2 NIM dip; analysts probed NIM trajectory, Motor Finance timing and capital needs.
